title.narrative: Women's Voice and Engagement (WOVEN) for Peace

description.narrative: This project will focus on women’s empowerment in the peacebuilding process ahead of the 2023 Presidential elections in Sierra Leone. The project will engage and train women and religious leaders in gender-sensitive ADR mechanisms, recognizing that gendered discrimination is inherently engrained in decision making and access to justice systems shaped by customary practice. The project will contribute to improving prevention of violence against women and girls through changes in knowledge, attitudes, and practices. The proposed initiative is relevant to the Sierra Leone/Liberia Programme Strategy and African Framework because it fits in with the key thematic areas of Women’s Economic, Social and Political Empowerment and Improved Governance, of which peacebuilding, especially before, during and after vulnerable election periods, is a critical priority. It fits in with the key characteristics of IEPM as it promotes the voices and agency of women in peace processes and engages communities in meaningful dialogue to enhance a culture of encounter with religious and women leaders. The project seeks to address issues of discriminatory structures and especially social discrimination against women by empowering them through social inclusion to bring about transformative change. Furthermore, by addressing peacebuilding needs to prevent conflicts, the project also seeks to respond to the cry of the poor and the earth.
